name: Parallelism sweep 1-256, 512 in / 256 out
description: As sweep-parallel-1-32-i512-o256-v1, continued to 64, 128 and 256 concurrent requests. Small models on a single accelerator are still scaling at 32 and 64 (google/gemma-4-E2B-it on a GB10 gained about 1.7x in output tokens per second from 16 to 32 concurrent requests while per-request decode slowed by only about 16 %), so the shorter sweeps end before the knee. This one finds it.
notes: Part of the small-model tier (workloads/README.md). Requests per sweep point = max(params.num_requests, concurrency * params.requests_per_concurrency): 32 up to concurrency 8, then 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024, 2,112 requests in all. A point only measures its concurrency if the engine admits that many sequences at once (vLLM --max-num-seqs, SGLang --max-running-requests, llama.cpp --parallel); record the value in args, because a lower cap turns the top points into queueing measurements (TTFT climbs, output_tok_s flattens). The m bucket holds 150 prompts, so from concurrency 64 up prompts repeat within a point: run with prefix caching off, or record that it was on, since cache hits shorten prefill. timeout_s is 600 because a request queued behind 255 others at a low sequence cap can legitimately wait minutes.
